data.title: PR 21: semantic neighbor generation with fail-closed coverage projection and exact budget continuation (re-review after cr-2r6hol)

data.body:
[HIGH][CWE-345] Public record mutation can forge projectable gate coverage. `NeighborhoodRecord` exposes `strategies`, `neighbors`, `failing`, and `verdict` as public mutable fields at lines 1077-1085. This method trusts those fields and never reconciles them. A caller can clear `failing`, change the verdict to `Complete`, and obtain schema-shaped coverage with zero disclosed failures. The original failed neighbors can remain in `neighbors` without affecting the projection.

Failure modes: A caller can publish false-green gate-5 coverage, omit known failures, or project unsupported work as complete.
Edge cases: Clearing only `failing` is sufficient. Editing counters, strategies, or the verdict creates further consistent-looking false results.
Rollback: Keep receipt and gate-5 wiring unavailable. Make result fields private and project only from a validated immutable record.
Monitoring: Independently compare neighbor dispositions, strategy counters, failing entries, and the derived verdict before receipt publication.
Validation: Mutate each public field after `explore`. Every doctored record must refuse projection and canonical evidence publication.
Counterevidence: Continuation decoding has a private consistency check. Ordinary `NeighborhoodRecord::receipt_coverage` does not call it.

[HIGH][CWE-345] Raw continuation bytes can rewrite committed failures into passes. `resume_bytes` accepts canonical JSON without an authenticated continuation identity or expected commitment. `check_consistent` at lines 2274-2335 only reconciles redundant fields. It explicitly delegates coherent-forgery protection to an external store. Resume clones recorded outcomes at lines 2621-2622. Prefix replay at lines 1680-1688 checks only candidate IDs and does not re-execute them. An attacker can change `Fail` to `Pass`, adjust counters, remove the failing entry, preserve the frontier, and later obtain `Complete` coverage.

Failure modes: Forged committed evidence can survive resume and support a false promotion receipt.
Edge cases: The attack needs a suspended campaign with a completed failing prefix. Canonical re-encoding does not prevent coherent edits.
Rollback: Disable raw-byte resume. Require a verified `cont_*` identity or signed commitment before decoding any committed outcome.
Monitoring: Record continuation commitments and reject every resume whose bytes do not match the authorized stored artifact.
Validation: Rewrite one committed failure and all redundant counts consistently. Resume must reject before any execution.
Counterevidence: The current forgery test changes only one redundant field at a time. It does not test a coherent rewrite.

[HIGH][CWE-345] Continuation reuse is not bound to semantic epochs or engine identity. The resume checks bind descriptive core and subject strings, envelope JSON, seed, selection, and generator knobs only. They omit `EpochSet`, engine identity, generator function version, core profile, and scenario edit commitments. Earlier strategy results are carried without replay at lines 2668-2673. Scenario replay accepts the same display ID even when its edit or profile changed.

Failure modes: A valid old continuation can mix stale committed evidence with results from new semantics, then finish as `Complete`.
Edge cases: A binary upgrade can keep the same subject and core strings. A substrate can reuse a scenario ID for changed semantics.
Rollback: Invalidate v0 continuations. Forbid resume until every consumed epoch, engine identity, and semantic candidate commitment is pinned.
Monitoring: Emit and compare epoch, engine, function, core-profile, and candidate commitments on every suspension and resume.
Validation: Resume across a changed engine and a same-ID changed scenario. Both cases must return a typed mismatch before reuse.
Counterevidence: The envelope and generator knobs are bound. They do not identify the evaluator or all semantic inputs. RFC 0030 lines 277-295 requires these pins.

[HIGH][CWE-345] The register substrate counts a different schedule as the requested neighbor. `run` compares the taken labels with `order` only when `exact` is true at lines 905-909. `realize` sets `exact` only for M01 schedule edits and always disables it for scenario edits at lines 963-974. The correct program therefore returns `Realized::Run` for its nearest schedule when the requested schedule is impossible. The campaign counts that run as executed and passed. The supported profile then projects `Complete` coverage. The golden evidence confirms only 46 distinct correct runs for 64 executed supported neighbors.

Failure modes: Unexecuted schedule neighbors become passing evidence and can create false-green coverage.
Edge cases: The correct program has fewer interleavings. Every deviating scenario order and collapsed schedule reaches this path.
Rollback: Withdraw the supported-profile receipt evidence. Return `NotRealizable` for any order mismatch, or prove an explicit equivalence relation before counting execution.
Monitoring: Compare requested and taken labels for every realization. Never increment `executed` when they differ.
Validation: Assert exact label equality for every schedule and scenario candidate. A mismatch must make projection inconclusive.
Counterevidence: The golden note discloses nearest-run behavior. The receipt schema has no approximation field, and `Complete` hides the gap.

[MEDIUM][CWE-754] Pending campaigns can be retyped as terminal inconclusive. This method checks undecided executions before it checks `Verdict::Pending`. If an earlier run was inconclusive and a later candidate exhausts budget, the record correctly remains pending with a continuation. Receipt projection instead returns `InconclusiveRuns`. Callers can therefore discard resumable work under the wrong typed outcome. Check `Pending` before any terminal projection refusal, and add a regression with an inconclusive prefix followed by budget exhaustion.

[MEDIUM][CWE-682] Scenario ID exhaustion leaks candidate budget. The campaign charges `meter.candidate(cost)` before asking the substrate for the ID. It then charges ID length separately at lines 1940-1941. If that second charge fails, the function returns without undoing the candidate charge. The continuation keeps no candidate, but its spend does. Repeated resume can charge the same frontier again and require a larger candidate ceiling than uninterrupted execution. Roll back the candidate charge on this path, or charge the complete predicted cost atomically. Test a long ID whose byte charge exhausts work.

[MEDIUM][CWE-190] Hostile continuation counts can panic instead of failing closed. `check_consistent` uses unchecked `sum::<u64>()` for rejection and not-realizable maps at lines 2293-2298. Canonical JSON permits several nonnegative `i64::MAX` counts. Three entries overflow `u64`, and workspace release builds enable overflow checks. `Continuation::decode` can therefore panic on untrusted bytes. Use checked sums and return `ResumeError::Malformed`. Add adversarial count tests at and above the overflow boundary.

data.body:
[HIGH][CWE-345] The replacement equivalence still counts a different causal schedule as the requested neighbor. `run` accepts when `same_interleaving` holds at lines 970-980. That relation drops every pair touching a label whose program-order prefix changed at lines 1020-1065 and 1102-1113. The retained evidence at tests/golden/pr21_impl01_neighborhood.evidence.txt:66-68 shows the result: the correct program constrains only 12 of 283 cross-actor pairs and zero dependent pairs. Thus `alternate-enabled-events` can be recorded as executed and passed without exercising the requested causal decision. The supported campaign still becomes `Complete` at lines 1720-1723 and projects this result.

Failure modes: A repair can move the operations around the defect, make them affected, collapse causal neighbors onto easier runs, and obtain false-green gate-5 coverage.
Edge cases: The current correct program already exempts every dependent pair. A repair that changes more program-order prefixes weakens the relation further.
Rollback: Do not publish the supported-profile projection. Treat schedule deviation as `NotRealizable`, or use a candidate-independent equivalence with a machine-checkable witness.
Monitoring: Record requested-versus-taken schedule commitments and the constrained dependent-pair count in the projectable evidence. Refuse zero dependent coverage for a selected causal strategy.
Validation: Add a repair that moves every causal-decision label while failing on one alternate order. The campaign must not become `Complete`.
Counterevidence: Disclosure in the golden note is not part of `coverage.neighborhood`; the projected JSON does not identify the weakened equivalence or its zero dependent-pair coverage.

[MEDIUM][CWE-754] Budget exhaustion still becomes terminal after an earlier engine error. An invalid run handle sets `engine_error` at lines 2371-2376. A later exhausted charge sets `exhausted` and a committed frontier at lines 3361-3365. This precedence selects `Inconclusive(EngineError)` before `Pending` at lines 3390-3397. The final match at lines 3429-3438 then returns `Finished` and discards the continuation. RFC 0032 requires every budget-exhausted campaign to remain pending with a continuation. Preserve the continuation whenever `exhausted` is true, and add a regression where an invalid handle precedes run-budget exhaustion.
[RESOLVED] `NeighborhoodRecord` fields are private at lines 1133-1145. Projection derives live inputs and reconciles all counts at lines 1605-1613.
[RESOLVED] Projection checks `Verdict::Pending` before terminal refusal at lines 1614-1618. The regression at tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:799-850 covers an undecided prefix followed by exhaustion.
[RESOLVED] The scenario path now reverses the candidate charge when string charging fails at lines 2571-2578. The long-identity regression is at tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:853-932.
[RESOLVED] Reconciliation uses checked addition at lines 1652-1659 and for aggregate totals. The hostile-count regression is at tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:634-673.
[RESOLVED] Untrusted bytes are decoded only for comparison with a fresh derivation at lines 3161-3198. No claimed outcome is resumed. The coherent-forgery regressions cover this path.

[RESOLVED] `Inputs` now binds the generator, transaction, subject, engine identity, core relation and profile, envelope, and configuration at lines 1250-1284. Per-candidate commitments include scenario bytes and profiles at lines 2319-2349, and replay compares them at lines 2260-2275.

data.body: [MEDIUM][CWE-400] Substrate outcome strings bypass the work budget. process charges a fixed MAX_HANDLE_BYTES reserve at lines 2367-2379, but dispose accepts arbitrary not-realizable reasons, unsupported reasons, property names, and run handles at lines 2450-2500. It clones several of them, retains all of them in the record, and later canonicalizes them without a cap or exact length charge. An oversized substrate response can therefore allocate an arbitrarily large record under a small remaining work budget. Invalid oversized handles are still retained after is_handle rejects them. Cap each outcome string before retention, or charge its exact byte length before cloning and return a typed engine error on exhaustion. Add boundary tests for oversized reasons, properties, and handles.

[HIGH][CWE-345] A fresh campaign treats a reused scenario identity as a duplicate without checking its semantic content. validate keys every non-schedule candidate only by cand.key at line 2311. process already computes the content commitment at line 2345, but a second scenario with the same identity and different edit bytes or profile becomes Rejected(Duplicate) and is never realized. Rejections do not create a coverage gap at lines 1852-1854, and the receipt projection omits them at lines 1947-1969. The campaign can therefore remain Complete and project while it silently skips a distinct failing neighbor.

Failure modes: An identity collision hides a semantic neighbor and creates false-green gate-5 coverage.
Edge cases: Same identity with different edit bytes, different profile, or both is unsafe. An exact identity-content duplicate can remain a normal duplicate.
Rollback: Refuse projection for scenario identity collisions until the duplicate check binds each identity to its first content commitment.
Monitoring: Record identity-to-commitment collisions and make any second commitment for one identity an engine error.
Validation: Enumerate two valid scenarios with one identity. Make the first pass and the second use different bytes or profile and fail. The campaign must become inconclusive or error, never Complete. Keep the existing exact-duplicate rejection test.

data.body: Fixed in 7480ed8f. Duplicates are now decided on a content address: a digest of the edit's canonical bytes and profile, excluding the identity. Coverage counts distinct content. A substrate identity is bound to the content it first came with. The same identity with other content is Rejection::IdentityCollision: it is never deduplicated, it sets engine_error so the verdict is Inconclusive(EngineError), reconcile keeps it from being Complete, and a resume rederives it (taints). An exact identity+content repeat stays Duplicate, and one content under two identities is one neighbor. Tests: a_forced_identity_collision_is_refused_and_never_complete (your case: same id, first passes, second has other bytes and fails, so EngineError and the projection is refused; exact-duplicate cases kept), scenario_coverage_counts_distinct_content_and_every_collision_is_an_error (200 random scenario lists vs a reference walk: kept neighbors have distinct content, and a collision rejection occurs iff an identity names two contents), and register every_scenario_identity_names_exactly_one_content (id<->content bijective over the corpus).

Fixed in 7480ed8f. Every substrate outcome string is bounded before it is kept: not-realizable and unsupported reasons, refuted properties (MAX_OUTCOME_BYTES=256) and run handles (MAX_HANDLE_BYTES=256). The run charge reserves handle + outcome + witness-check work before realize. A longer string is never copied: only its length is read, it is replaced by the typed marker OVERSIZED plus its length, and the outcome keeps its kind (Pass/Fail/NotRealizable/Unsupported). The campaign becomes Inconclusive(EngineError) and is rederived on resume. Witness vectors longer than the core are refused before iteration. Test: oversized_outcome_strings_are_bounded_and_make_the_campaign_an_engine_error. With 1 MiB reasons, properties and handles, the kinds are unchanged, the markers are present, the record is under 64 KiB, the projection is refused, and a work budget one unit short of the reserve suspends with 0 runs.

[HIGH][CWE-345] Remains open at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:2350-2363. The code binds cand.key only when seen_content.insert succeeds. Sequence a/X, b/X, b/Y accepts a/X, treats b/X as Duplicate without binding b, then accepts b/Y as fresh. The record can become Complete and project although identity b named two canonical contents. The randomized reference repeats the same conditional insertion at crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:2245-2256, so it misses this case.

Failure modes: An alias-first identity collision escapes the engine-error taint and produces false-green complete coverage.
Edge cases: The first sighting of the reused identity must duplicate content already seen under another identity; a later new content then escapes.
Rollback: Refuse projection until every first-seen identity is bound before global content deduplication.
Monitoring: Reconcile every raw scenario identity against exactly one content, including candidates rejected as content duplicates.
Validation: Test a/X, b/X, b/Y. The third candidate must be IdentityCollision and the campaign must not be Complete.
Counterevidence: The direct two-entry collision test is fixed, but it does not exercise an alias-first identity.

[MEDIUM][CWE-400] Remains open. The new caps cover realize and execute outputs, but selected-strategy NotRun reasons are still copied directly into the record at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:3589-3592 without a cap or byte charge. The identity charge is also detached from storage: charge_strings calls and discards three values at lines 1385-1393, then Inputs::build calls the methods again at lines 1325, 1330, and 1333. A stateful substrate can return short charged values and arbitrarily large stored values. These paths still let record size exceed the work budget. Capture and charge the exact stored strings once, bound NotRun reasons, mark oversize as EngineError, and add adversarial tests for both paths.

data.reason: BLOCK: HIGH alias-first scenario identity collisions can still project Complete, and MEDIUM substrate string paths can still exceed the work budget.

data.body: Fixed structurally in a8c83a85. Identity and content now form an order-independent bijection per strategy. Both maps are kept (id_to_content, content_to_id). Every declared non-schedule pair, including one the envelope later rejects, is bound before any other check. An exact repeat is Duplicate; any second binding in either direction (one identity with two contents, or one content under two identities, which covers your a/X, b/X, b/Y) is IdentityCollision, an engine error. reconcile holds Complete to a whole-set bijection over every content-addressed neighbor, rejected ones included (the identity may be empty; selection is by content address). A non-bijection must carry a collision rejection, or the record is inconsistent. The profile has one canonical spelling: zero counts are dropped and max_value is exact. Tests: the_identity_content_check_does_not_depend_on_arrival_order runs 150 random lists mixing aliases, collisions, exact duplicates and envelope-rejected pairs, over every permutation. The verdict is identical for all orders, Complete iff the distinct pairs are a bijection (and something runs), and a collision is recorded iff they are not. a_forced_identity_collision_is_refused_and_never_complete now also covers the alias case and a/X,b/X,b/Y. an_empty_scenario_identity_is_an_identity_like_any_other and one_profile_has_one_spelling come from the fresh opus adversarial pass.

Fixed structurally in a8c83a85. I enumerated every entry point. The Substrate trait supplies core_identity, subject, engine_identity, core_profile, not_run (NotRun), the scenario tuple (id, S, Profile), scenario_bytes, and realize (NotRealizable, Unsupported, Witness::Edit, Witness::Schedule). execute supplies the Pass/Fail property and handle. CausalCore supplies len, hard_predecessors, dependent, in_core and class. Now: (1) the core is read exactly once into a charged, checked snapshot (Frozen); every later query and the commitment use the snapshot, never the substrate's core. (2) core_profile and the three identities are read once, and what is charged is what is bound (Identities); Inputs::of envelope-checks the profile it reads. (3) Every string or byte vector goes through admit/admit_copies, which reads the length, refuses past the cap without copying (a typed OVERSIZED marker, or CoreError::IdentityTooLong for identities), and charges length times the copies kept. The run reserve now covers 3 handle copies and 2 reason/property copies. NotRun reasons are admitted. Tests: every_substrate_string_entry_point_is_bounded_at_a_mebibyte walks all 12 string entry points at 1 MiB. identities_are_read_once_and_bound_as_charged uses a stateful substrate. the_core_and_its_profile_are_read_once_and_used_as_checked (from the adversarial pass) drifts predecessors and profile after the first read: they are read once, spend stays within budget, the checked profile is bound, and the verifier's fresh read is refused, typed.

[RESOLVED] The repair now binds both directions before envelope validation at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:2557-2572. Reconciliation checks the full recorded pair set at lines 2021-2058. The alias-first sequence a/X, b/X, b/Y is covered at crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:2193-2226.

data.body:
[HIGH][CWE-345] The causal-neighbor witness check ignores hard-order edges. Candidate validation treats each hard edge as an ordering constraint at lines 2352-2367, and check_class treats it as a conflict at lines 2500-2504. This check compares only core.dependent at lines 2901-2905. A full non-halted witness can reverse a hard-only program-order or message edge, pass the decision check, execute, and count toward Complete coverage. For example, with hard edge 0->1 and no dependent pairs, requested swap(1,2) is [0,2,1], but witness [2,1,0] satisfies decision 2 before 1 while reversing 0->1.

Failure modes: A faulty or hostile substrate can turn a different, causally invalid run into passing gate-5 evidence and project false-green coverage.
Edge cases: The defect requires a hard-only pair. Program-order edges in the register core have this shape. Full non-halted witnesses remain affected.
Rollback: Keep schedule-neighbor receipt projection unavailable until witness validation checks self.facts.hard_edge together with dependence.
Monitoring: Count and disclose requested-versus-taken hard-edge inversions before any run becomes Executed.
Validation: Add a three-event core with hard 0->1, no dependence, requested [0,2,1], and witness [2,1,0]. It must become NotRealizable and never Complete.
Counterevidence: The current register scheduler preserves actor order, but this public generic library claims to own the causal-neighbor check. The independent reference at tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:1649-1674 repeats the same omission.

[MEDIUM][CWE-345] Semantic equality is decided only by BLAKE3 digests, contrary to ADR-0013. content hashes the canonical edit and profile at lines 2730-2755, then the identity maps decide Duplicate or IdentityCollision solely from that digest at lines 2557-2571. The core binding likewise retains only the relation digest at line 2333. Two distinct canonical values with one digest can therefore suppress a neighbor or make a stale core appear current. With the same scenario identity, the second colliding edit is classified Duplicate, never realized, and a record can remain Complete. ADR-0013 requires hashes to index buckets and collisions to resolve by exact canonical comparison. Retain canonical bytes for equality, or label this as probabilistic non-certified evidence and prohibit its use for promotion.

data.reason: BLOCK: HIGH hard-order witness inversions can count causally invalid runs as Complete coverage; MEDIUM digest-only semantic equality violates ADR-0013 exact comparison.

data.body: Fixed in 11c2b4ab. The witness check now holds a realization to the core's hard order as a transitive closure: Frozen::ancestors bitsets, built and charged once in check_core. Every taken event's hard ancestors must have been taken before it or be absent from the program. That refuses a direct or transitive inversion, one through an absent middle event, and, in a halted run, an event taken while a hard ancestor the program has is still pending. Only the declared decision deviates, and the generator already refuses any candidate that inverts a hard edge (check_schedule over full permutations, so the closure too). Typed reason: 'witness: a hard edge inverted'. Tests: a_witness_that_inverts_a_hard_edge_is_refused_and_never_complete (your 3-event core: requested [0,2,1], witness [2,1,0], NotRealizable, never Complete); a_transitive_hard_inversion_through_an_absent_event_is_refused; a_halted_run_cannot_take_an_event_before_a_pending_hard_ancestor (from the fresh opus pass); and the property no_executed_neighbor_inverts_a_hard_edge_and_no_candidate_proposes_one, against an independent reference that checks the closure. Register: the correct program now realizes only its 34 scenario neighbors, and the evidence and START_HERE say so.

Fixed in 11c2b4ab, per ADR-0013 (hashes index, collisions resolve by exact comparison). (1) Scenario identity/content: both bijection maps are keyed and compared on the canonical content bytes (edit bytes + canonical profile). The digest decides neither equality nor inequality; a digest seen with other bytes is Rejection::DigestCollision, an engine error that never projects. (2) Resume replay compares each committed candidate's content bytes (kept in the in-process Continuation) as well as the commitment. (3) The core binding carries its canonical relation text beside the digest, and staleness compares it exactly. (4) Each witness is recorded as canonical text, not a digest. (5) The content index is bound into Inputs; a verifier's derivation says blake3, so a record made through the test hook (explore_with_content_index) is Stale and never projects. The record's reconcile works on digests because it has no bytes; the fresh opus pass confirmed collisions are caught before anything is recorded, and resume_untrusted always returns the fresh derivation. Tests: a_forced_digest_collision_is_decided_on_the_bytes (one-bucket index: DigestCollision, never Complete; the same bytes stay Duplicate), no_content_index_decides_equality_or_inequality_and_a_hook_record_never_projects (a stateful index still gives the collision; a hook record is Stale{content_index}), and the_core_binding_and_the_witness_are_kept_as_canonical_text.

[RESOLVED] Exact canonical bytes now decide identity and content equality at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:2645-2679. A digest collision becomes a tainting rejection, core relation text is bound at lines 1368-1375, and the test index cannot project.

data.body: [RESOLVED] check_core builds the charged transitive hard-ancestor closure at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:2359-2378. check_witness requires every taken event ancestor to be taken earlier or absent at lines 3036-3051, including halted runs.

data.body: [MEDIUM][CWE-400] Canonical scenario content is retained several times but charged once. scenarios charges scenario_bytes once at lines 3280-3285. validate then clones the combined content into id_to_content, content_to_id, and by_digest at lines 2668-2674, and process retains a fourth copy in contents at line 2837. resume clones the complete contents corpus at line 4037 and clones the current strategy again into replay at lines 4137-4150, without a byte charge. A substrate can supply many unique 65,536-byte edits and force memory use several times larger than the declared work budget, including when little resume budget remains. Store canonical content once behind shared immutable storage, or charge every retained and resume-time copy before allocation. Add a max-size multi-candidate regression that proves suspension occurs before every copy the budget cannot pay for, including resume.

data.reason: Unresolved [MEDIUM][CWE-400]: scenario canonical bytes and continuation content are retained through multiple uncharged clones, so memory can exceed the declared work budget. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

data.body: Fixed in 20a2926a by sharing, not accounting. Each candidate's canonical content (edit bytes plus canonical profile) is built once as one Arc<[u8]>. The id-to-content and content-to-id bijection maps, the digest index, the committed contents, the continuation and the replay comparison each hold a pointer to it, so the bytes are stored once. Charging: the scenario edit bytes are admitted with 2 copies (the candidate's transient copy and the shared content), the profile part is a bounded constant in every candidate's cost, and a schedule's order is within its candidate cost; all of it before the content is built. The suspended record is one Arc shared by the outcome and its continuation, never cloned; the regeneration-exhausted path shares the prior record and contents instead of copying. The witness text (at most 8 bytes per core event plus a frame) is within the run reserve. A resume charges the committed neighbors and failing list it copies, by retained size, before copying, and refuses with ResumeError::Exhausted otherwise. Test: retained_content_bytes_are_charged_before_they_are_kept. 50 scenario edits of 60 KiB (3 MiB) under a 1 MiB budget suspend. From the lengths, the continuation keeps exactly one allocation per committed content, whose bytes are at most the charged work and at most the budget. Resumed with room, it completes with spend at least the 3 MiB kept. A counting allocator is not possible: GlobalAlloc needs unsafe, which the workspace forbids. The test measures the retained bytes through Continuation::retained_content (doc-hidden), counting each allocation once.

[RESOLVED] Canonical content is now one Arc allocation built at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:2756-2761 and shared by the maps, retained contents, and replay at lines 2694-2702 and 4222-4235. Scenario admission charges the transient edit plus retained content before construction at lines 3316-3325.

[MEDIUM][CWE-400] A resume that exhausts while regenerating committed candidates discards all regeneration spend. This branch returns the prior record and continuation unchanged, although core checking, identity derivation, record-copy charging, and candidate regeneration already consumed work. The next resume starts again from the old spent value at line 4059. Repeating the same insufficient cumulative budget therefore repeats bounded work indefinitely while the returned ledger never advances, bypassing RFC 0032 cumulative per-transaction cost accounting. Persist the added spend without duplicating retained content, and add a regression that repeatedly resumes with a budget that reaches partway through replay. Each returned ledger must advance monotonically, or the operation must refuse before repeating unaccounted work.

[HIGH][CWE-190] Saturating profile addition can admit a generated neighbor outside the protected fault bound. Profile::with_fault saturates at lines 527-530, and merged uses it here before Envelope::check. With a core profile containing u32::MAX duplication faults and bounds.faults = u32::MAX, the generated duplicate-message neighbor adds one fault but remains u32::MAX. The envelope accepts it at lines 591-605, so the run can contribute to Complete coverage although its real profile exceeds intent. DeclaredBound carries i64, so the type does not exclude this boundary.

Failure modes: Gate 5 can execute and project a neighbor that violates the Intent Contract, producing false-green protected-intent evidence.
Edge cases: The bypass applies when Delay, Duplication, or Loss is already u32::MAX and the generic generator adds one. The cancellation saturation has the same unsafe merge behavior if a generic cancellation is added later.
Rollback: Refuse projection until profile composition uses checked arithmetic and turns overflow into a typed rejection or engine error.
Monitoring: Record profile-merge overflow with the class, base count, and added count. Treat any occurrence as a non-projectable engine defect.
Validation: Use a one-send core with duplication enabled, core Duplication = u32::MAX, and faults bound = u32::MAX. The generated duplicate must be rejected before realization and the campaign must not become Complete.

data.body: Fixed at class level. Composition is checked end to end. merged() now returns Result and uses checked_add on every fault class, cancellation and node/value quantity. Profile::with_fault keeps u32::MAX as an unrepresentable marker instead of a clamp, and checked_with_fault returns None. Envelope::check refuses any u32::MAX count as the typed Rejection::ProfileOverflow{class}, token profile-overflow. That is an envelope rejection, so the candidate is never realized or admitted. It also refuses recoveries > crashes (ExceedsFaultBound{Recoveries}). I grepped the crate for saturating_/wrapping_/unchecked + and * on bounded quantities. The undecided/executed folds, the witness length check (checked_add, is_none_or) and retained_content (u128 sum) are now checked. Two remaining uses are justified in comments. SplitMix wrapping is PRNG mixing, not a quantity. Meter cost saturation only goes upward and exceeds any admissible budget (≤ i64::MAX), so it refuses and never admits. New tests: a_fault_count_that_overflows_is_refused_never_admitted (your u32::MAX duplication core plus a generated duplicate: refused, never realized); no_admitted_neighbor_exceeds_any_envelope_bound (property over seeds, cores and envelopes); recoveries_never_exceed_the_crashes_they_complete.

Fixed. Spend is cumulative across every path, and nothing restarts from an old value. When a resume exhausts while regenerating committed candidates, it rebuilds the pending record from the campaign's committed copies with spent = the meter's cumulative total, plus a continuation at the same frontier. So the next resume starts from the larger spend. The adversarial pass found a second reset. An exhaustion while reading a not-run reason before the prior frontier ended as a terminal EngineError. It now takes the same rebuild_pending path. A resume that cannot progress (work ≤ spent.work, candidates ≤ spent.candidates, or runs < spent.runs) is refused as ResumeError::Exhausted before any work, so an exhausted state cannot be retried for free. resume_untrusted charges the bytes it reads into the fresh derivation's ledger (initial_work) instead of taking them off the budget. New tests: repeated_exhausted_resumes_advance_the_ledger_and_never_repeat_free_work (exhaust/resume cycles: spend is monotone, equals the sum of actual work, and stays within the declared budgets); every_exhaustion_before_the_prior_frontier_suspends_with_the_committed_state (sweeps 30k work budgets: never EngineError, the frontier never moves back); a_resume_that_cannot_progress_is_refused_before_any_work; an_untrusted_resume_records_the_bytes_it_reads.

[HIGH][CWE-682][CWE-345] Remains open at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:527-579 and 3456-3466. The repair reserves u32::MAX as an overflow marker even though u32::MAX is an exact representable count and the Intent bound is i64. With a core duplication count of u32::MAX - 1 and bounds.faults = u32::MAX, adding one duplication is valid. checked_add succeeds to the exact bound, then Envelope::check rejects that value as ProfileOverflow. Rejections do not taint the record at lines 1497-1510 or create a gap at lines 4429-4464, so other executed message neighbors can still yield Complete and project. The regression at crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:3578-3587 explicitly blesses this false rejection.

Failure modes: A repair can fail only at the protected maximum and receive false-green gate-5 coverage because that valid boundary neighbor is skipped.
Edge cases: Direct profiles containing exactly u32::MAX are also refused. The same defect applies to cancellations at the exact maximum.
Rollback: Use widened or tagged composition. Admit exact u32::MAX when it is within the Intent bound. Represent only checked_add failure as overflow.
Monitoring: Record actual checked-add overflow separately from ordinary bound rejection. Treat any generated representational gap as non-projectable.
Validation: Admit u32::MAX - 1 plus one under a u32::MAX bound. Reject u32::MAX plus one. Run a campaign where the exact-bound neighbor is the only failure and require disclosure.
Counterevidence: The new code prevents the original saturating clamp from admitting an over-bound neighbor, but it now drops an in-bound neighbor at the exact maximum.

[MEDIUM][CWE-400] Remains open before Campaign construction at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:4192-4218. The precheck only requires the new work ceiling to exceed prior spend. check_core, identity admission, or committed-record copy reservation can then consume local meter work and return ResumeError::Exhausted. No rebuilt continuation carries that spend. Repeating the same continuation and insufficient budget repeats the same work while the cumulative ledger stays unchanged. rebuild_pending fixes exhaustion after Campaign exists, but not these earlier paths. Return a pending continuation with the advanced ledger for every post-precheck exhaustion, or precharge the exact full preflight before any work. Add boundary tests that force exhaustion inside core checking, each identity read, and committed-copy reservation, then repeat the same call and prove no work repeats.

[MEDIUM][CWE-400] Untrusted continuation failures also bypass cumulative accounting. resume_untrusted checks length and parses at crates/continuum-repair/src/neighborhood.rs:4126-4130 before any persistent ledger exists. A late malformed document returns without recording parse work. A well-formed forged document can force the fresh derivation at lines 4133-4141, then fail comparison at lines 4150-4162, again returning no record or continuation with the charged work. The same bytes can therefore repeat parsing or a full derivation under an unchanged transaction ledger. The success-only regression does not cover malformed or forged exits. Persist the attempt spend on every exit, or require an outer cumulative meter and make that contract explicit and enforced.

data.body: Fixed at 651edc5c. The u32::MAX marker is gone. Profile composition is checked in u64: a Wide profile, where two u32 counts always sum exactly. So there is no overflow, no clamp, and no ProfileOverflow; that variant is removed. with_fault is checked and returns None past u32::MAX. Every bound is inclusive: faults, the crash, cancellation and partition caps, nodes, and recoveries <= crashes. values is a count, so index bound-1 is admitted. Your case: u32::MAX-1 plus one under a u32::MAX bound is admitted; u32::MAX plus one is refused as ExceedsFaultBound with its true count; the same is admitted under a u32::MAX+1 bound. Coverage: a new exhaustive Rejection::is_engine_error, plus one engine_refusal rule shared by the campaign and taints(), makes any refusal of a candidate the intent may permit a coverage gap (EngineError, never Complete). This covers identity or digest collision, oversized, malformed core, and a schedule refusal in the hoist or delay generators. The adversarial pass found two generators that dropped permitted neighbors as ViolatesCausalOrder while staying Complete: a hoist behind a hard ancestor, and a delay past the send's own successor. The hoist now carries j's hard ancestors (transitive), and the delay moves the send past its next non-descendant events; both are valid by construction. The register evidence recovers 8 neighbors: M01 now fails on 74 of 80, and the supported profile stays Complete. A halted run is now decided before its outcome strings, so resumed and uninterrupted records match. Tests: an_exact_bound_is_admitted_and_one_past_it_is_refused_as_outside_the_envelope; an_exact_bound_neighbor_is_executed_and_disclosed_and_an_engine_refusal_is_never_complete; only_refusals_outside_the_envelope_or_of_non_neighbors_leave_a_campaign_complete; no_admitted_neighbor_exceeds_any_envelope_bound (now also asserts that every refusal passes a bound); a_decision_behind_a_hard_ancestor_is_hoisted_with_it_and_taken; a_delay_moves_the_send_past_independent_events_not_its_own_successor; every_permitted_decision_and_delay_is_generated_and_none_is_dropped_as_invalid; a_halted_run_is_decided_before_its_outcome_and_resumes_to_the_same_result.

Fixed at 651edc5c. resume now takes the caller's cumulative ledger (&mut Spent) as an explicit outer meter. The attempt starts from the larger of the ledger's work and the continuation's. It is refused before any work when the budget has nothing left above that. run_campaign owns the meter, and the Campaign borrows it, so the Campaign is built with the carried spend, never zero. The meter's total is written back to the ledger on every exit: core-check, identity-read and committed-copy exhaustion before the Campaign exists, Mismatch, Diverged, suspension and finish. Repeating the same call with the same ledger therefore either advances it by the work actually done or is refused before any substrate call. Candidates and runs remain the record's counts, because reconcile holds them to its neighbors; re-executed work is paid in work. Tests: exhaustion_before_the_campaign_exists_is_charged_and_never_repeated_for_free sweeps every budget from committed+1 to +3000 and repeats each call 4 times; it asserts the ledger is monotone and within budget, and that a refusal is followed by no work. repeated_exhausted_resumes_advance_the_ledger_and_never_repeat_free_work repeats each call 3 times with a persistent ledger.

Fixed at 651edc5c. resume_untrusted takes the caller's ledger (&mut Spent) and never takes the bytes' claimed spend into it, so forged bytes cannot inflate or deflate it. check_budget runs first. The length is charged to the ledger before the first byte is read, and only if work remains after it. The fresh derivation's meter starts from that ledger, and the total is written back on every exit: Malformed (the bytes read), Mismatch and Forged (the full derivation), suspension and finish. A retry with the same ledger is refused before reading once the budget is spent. Test: untrusted_resumes_charge_every_byte_and_check_and_the_ledger_is_monotone. It covers a chain of untrusted resumes from the returned bytes, where the ledger strictly advances by more than the bytes read and equals the record's spend. It also covers malformed, forged and mismatched exits, which keep their spend, and a refusal with nothing left, which leaves the ledger unchanged.
